answer_1.quote: We investigate three scenarios (Fig.  (1) an Editing model that aligns initial system outputs to human demonstrations based on the user feedback; (2) a Critic model that predicts user feedback of initial system outputs according to the user requirements; (3) an Editor model that automatically aligns the initial system outputs to user needs by predicting both the user feedback and edited summary.
answer_1.outputs: system-generated summaries, human-edited summaries, human feedback (explanation, evidence, instructions)

answer_2.quote: To evaluate the factual consistency, we use two automatic metrics, DAE  and QAFactEval , which achieve strong performance on the XSum dataset .

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation on the quality of model-edited summaries. We ask the annotators two questions: (1) Are the generated summaries more factually consistent than the original summaries (yes/no); (2) Do the generated summaries follow the instructions (yes/partly/no). We randomly sampled 100 examples from the test set, and have each generated summary annotated by three MTurk annotators.
answer_4.guideline: Are the generated summaries more factually consistent than the original summaries (yes/no); Do the generated summaries follow the instructions (yes/partly/no).
